extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students and researchers interested in French literature
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic survey of French literature: definitions, historical periods, major movements, key texts, authors, and prominent literary awards. Intended as a broad reference/starting point for study or general interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of French literature
rubrics_metrics.description: "French literature (French: littérature française) generally speaking, is literature written in the French language, particularly by French citizens; it may also refer to literature written by people living in France who speak traditional languages of France other than French."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This passage establishes the scope of what the article treats as 'French literature' — emphasising language (French) and a primary association with French citizens or residents writing in regional languages of France.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Francophone literature
rubrics_metrics.description: "Literature written in the French language by citizens of other nations such as Belgium, Switzerland, Canada, Senegal, Tunisia, Algeria, Morocco, etc. is referred to as Francophone literature."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes literature in French produced outside France (by non‑French citizens) as 'Francophone literature', thereby separating national from linguistic/colonial spheres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation / verifiability requirement (Wikipedia)
rubrics_metrics.description: "This article needs additional citations for verification. Please help improve this article by adding citations to reliable sources. Unsourced material may be challenged and removed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A content-quality standard applying to the article itself: statements should be supported by reliable sources; unsourced claims are liable to challenge or removal. (This is an editorial requirement for the Wikipedia page rather than a literary criterion.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand Prix de Littérature Policière scope
rubrics_metrics.description: "Grand Prix de Littérature Policière – created in 1948, for crime and detective fiction."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award-specific eligibility/criterion: the prize is intended for works in the crime/detective fiction genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prix Goncourt awarding criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Prix Goncourt – created 1903, given to the author of 'the best and most imaginative prose work of the year'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the evaluative standard for this major French prize: judged on being the 'best and most imaginative' prose work published that year (prose, rather than poetry or other forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prix Médicis awarding criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Prix Médicis – created 1958, awarded to an author whose 'fame does not yet match their talent.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the prize as targeting relatively under‑recognized authors whose talent exceeds their current fame — an esthetic/recognition-based criterion rather than strict genre or form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prix Tour-Apollo eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: "Prix Tour-Apollo Award – 1972–1990, given to the best science fiction novel published in French during the preceding year."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies temporal and linguistic eligibility (published in French during the preceding year) and genre (science fiction), with selection based on being 'the best' of that cohort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prix Femina jury composition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Prix Femina – created 1904, decided each year by an exclusively female jury, although the authors of the winning works do not have to be women."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A structural rule about how the prize is decided: an all-female jury selects the winner, but there is no gender requirement for winners; this is a procedural/selection criterion rather than a literary-content one.
